articleTitle: Time to flashover characteristics and flashover mechanisms of a liquid film
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The origin of the phenomenon under study is the problem of flashover of high voltage polluted insulators,<sup>1</sup> where a discharge elongates at the surface of a conducting film created by pollution deposition and humidification. The process ends up in a complete short circuit of the insulator.

articleTitle: Effects of hydrated ions on water trees in polyethylene
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The results of the present study suggest that ionic contaminants, if present not only in the insulation but also on the surface of outer and inner semiconductive layers, accelerate the generation and growth of water trees. In cable production, therefore, care should be exercised so as to choose cable insulation and semiconductor materials that contain as little low S<sup>0</sup> ions (e.g., OH<sup>−</sup>, SO<inf>4</inf><sup>2−</sup>, Na<sup>+</sup>, Ca<sup>2+</sup>, etc.) as possible.

articleTitle: Conductive anodic filaments (CAF): An electrochemical failure mechanism of reinforced polymeric dielectrics
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: An electrochemical failure mechanism (CAF) of rigid polymeric dielectrics has been discussed. The life of a printed-circuit board composed of CAF - susceptible material is a function of temperature, humidity and applied bias. Although an electrochemical corrosion of the metallic conductors is the ultimate result of the process, the integrity of the resin/glass interface may be the life-limiting property of the material.

articleTitle: Formative time lag in small gaps with nearly homogeneous field distribution
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: For high overvoltages the discharge formation in SF<inf>6</inf> develops in a similar way as in non-electronegative gases. In this range the formative time lags are nearly inversely proportional to the pressure-reduced field strengths E/p. Due to the high field strengths and the high electron energies in this range of overvoltage, the probability of electron attachment is very low.<sup>4</sup> Thus, the electronegative characteristics of SF<inf>6</inf> get lost.

articleTitle: Evidence for the role of free volume in the high field breakdown of polymers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The characteristic sharp reduction in electric strength exhibited by most polymeric materials at a critical temperature, T<inf>c</inf>, is well documented.<sup>1, 2</sup> There is substantial agreement that the low temperature breakdown mechanism is likely to be electronic in nature. A number of theories have been proposed although they all have the common feature that an indefinitely large electron multiplication determines the eventual destruction of the material. Of these theories, perhaps that due to Fröhlich<sup>3</sup> has been the most successful and has been adapted to describe both amorphous materials and events in the temperature region above T<inf>c</inf>, where the density of conduction electrons is sufficiently high to make interaction with trapped electrons the preferred energy exchange process. To a first approximation the electric strength, E, decreases on the basis of a Fröhlich model according to the relation, equation

articleTitle: The influence of extruded semiconducting shields on the contamination of XLPE cables
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Nuetron activation is a powerful tool to determine the average concentrations of contaminants in XLPE aged cables. It also allows the determination of radial contaminant profiles in full size cables. Semiconducting shields appear to act as sources of contamination in XLPE cables. The increase of tan δ in thermally aged cables could be due to the presence of ionic impurities; one cannot exclude, however, the possibility of oxidation effects. More work is needed to establish clearly a relation between contamination and treeing.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated decay of negatively charged Teflon - FEP
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) of polymers has become a widely used experimental technique for the investigation of various material parameters, such as charge storage properties,<sup>1</sup> surface voltage stability,<sup>2–3</sup> determination of the mean depth of the internal charge,<sup>4</sup> activation energies<sup>5</sup> of traps and the trap structure<sup>6</sup> of the material.

articleTitle: The determination of trace contaminants in polymers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Although not as successful as anticipated, this first study has shown several pitfalls in the determination of trace ions not previously anticipated. It has shown (1) the presence of trace amounts of starting materials or hydrolysis products, both of which attack metallurgy; (2) elements present in the polymer are not always extractable and, therefore, not mobile; (3) pure materials may be contaminated by their containers; (4) several simultaneous analytical methods are necessary, since each has unique properties.

articleTitle: A new sample configuration for short-time and endurance tests of extruded insulation
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The extruded sample configuration presented in this paper has enabled a better representation of cable designs and has proved a valuable aid in studying thermoplastic materials' dielectric behavior under multistress conditions.

articleTitle: Triple junction: Metal-gas-solid dielectric
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: A solid spacer usually constitutes a weak point in any insulation system with quasi-uniform field, even if its surfaces coincide at every point with the field lines of the gap. This lowering of the flashover voltage can only be attributed to the introduction of local field non-uniformities at the spacer surface, leading to premature discharges in the gas. Various experiments have been conducted on the surface discharges of spacers, but results differ widely among authors, so that it is still difficult to evaluate univocally the influence of a particular parameter on the spacer strength. This study was undertaken to investigate some of these concerns.

articleTitle: The influence of electrode material upon prebreakdown current in viscous dielectric oil
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Silicone fluids are now being used as an insulator. Watson,<sup>2</sup> Hakim,<sup>3</sup> and Hosticka<sup>4</sup> have carried out some investigations on this liquid. There is still, however, a great deal that is unclear about the breakdown mechanism under high electric field. It is of importance to know the behavior of the current stress characteristic in the region below breakdown, since the breakdown itself in the liquid dielectric is the ultimate point of the conduction stage.<sup>1</sup> It is, therefore, worthwhile characterizing more fully their dielectric performance in this region of electric field. Watson<sup>2</sup> has studied the influence of electrode separation upon current conduction in silicone oil and has shown that a linear relationship between the slope of the log voltage vs. log current [d(ℓnV)/d(ℓnI)] ani gap separation exists. He has also shown this phenomenon to be consistent with a model involving Fowler-Nordheim emission which initiates a convective charge transport mechanism with the fluid flowing in a vortex cell enclosing a steady irrotational funnel flow through its core at the cathode. In his interpretation, negative charge will be trapped in the moving core of liquid dielectric, and the space charge is contained laterally by the tendency of the vortex ring to resist stretching by the outward component of the electrostatic Maxwell stress. He reports that the Maxwell stress from this space charge will increase and enlarge the vortex by raising the applied voltage. This suggests that the phenomenon may be influenced by the viscosity of the liquid. The effect of electrode materials was also considered from the viewpoint of their capability to inject charge under stress.

articleTitle: Charge buildup during electron irradiation
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: In recent years, several methods for the analysis of charge buildup in dielectrics during irradiation with a nonpenetrating electron beam have been developed. The most elementary model assuming a single range of electrons has been proposed by Gross et al. [1) in 1974. Two years later, Matsuoka et al. [2) included range straggling of electrons using experimental electron deposition and depth-dose curves. In 1979 Berkley [3) used a Monte Carlo simulation for the irradiation parameters to solve the nonlinear transport equation. In the same year Tanaka et al. [4) measured the reduction of the electron range due to space charge accumulation. Recently Gross et al. [5) generalized the original box model introducing a time dependent conductivity. In the present paper the different theoretical approaches are outlined and compared with each other for three boundary conditions. Additionally a modified box model including time dependent range of electrons is suggested.

articleTitle: Photo electron emission from dielectric materials by ultra-violet-ray irradiation
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Photo-electron-emission from polymer films by u.v. irradiation was investigated for the better understanding of the surface discharge mechanisms. Emitted electron current was measured for PE, PP, PS, and PETP. The results are as follows: • The number of electrons emitted was about 10<sup>6</sup> per irradiated area/sec. • It was found that materials containing benzene muclei tend to emit many electrons. • The threshold energy for electron emission for each material was determined as 5.5 eV, approximately.

articleTitle: Surface flashover strength in supercritical helium
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Table 1 shows the surface flashover fields and their standard deviations in the liquid and supercritical helium. According to the authors' experiments,<sup>3</sup> the flashover fields of the liquid and supercritical helium for dc voltage are 27 MV m<sup>−1</sup> and 55 MV m<sup>−1</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Detection of electric field at the interface of dielectrics and electrode by measuring electric stress
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: It is believed that the newly developed acoustic Maxwell stress sensor presented in this paper is a useful tool for the investigation of the interfacial electric field. We have successfully demonstrated the usefulness for amorphous insulating polymers such as PET, PVDF, and PE. We are presently improving the accuracy, range, and resolution of the equipment and studying its applicability to various liquid insulators and ferro-electrics.

articleTitle: Prebreakdown events and breakdown involving solid-liquid interfaces
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Recently, we have correlated impulse strength of oils with measurements of prebreakdown streamer velocities.<sup>1</sup> This paper extends such work to composite solid-liquid systems. The methods for measuring streamer velocities by shadowgraphy have been described previously.<sup>2</sup> The creepage fixture utilizes two cylindrical electrodes (1.27 cm diameter) resting on the solid dielectric whose other surface is a ground plane (cf. Figure 1). In order to facilitate streamer initiation, a 3 µm radius point was inset into the high voltage electrode to protrude 0.5 mm into the gap, 0.25 mm above the insulating surface. Because shadowgraphy requires transparency, most work has been done using a polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) slab with an indium-tin oxide transparent ground electrode. In one case, streamer velocities were measured on paper by laying 10 µm thick capacitor tissue on the PMMA surface, adhesion being provided by the surface tension of the oil.

articleTitle: Multiple morphologies in cross-linked polyethylene
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Here, a radial section of an uncross-linked miniature extruded cable was studied, the cable having been polished and cut in half, and then each half treated with one etchant. Both etchants revealed the spherulitic structure (Figure 1), much greater penetration having occurred in the case of the permanganic etchant. The general distribution of sizes of spherulites revealed by each technique was similar, confirming that molecules easily removed from spherulite boundaries by organic solvent are amorphous in character.

articleTitle: Flashover of resistor and varistor materials
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Typical voltage waveforms observed when a zinc oxide particle was stressed to breakdown are shown in Figure 1. The three different waveforms correspond to applying the voltage at three widely different rates of rise by varying the pulse amplitude. At the lowest rate, a fraction of a microsecond was required before sufficient conductivity was attained to collapse the voltage. A more abrupt collapse resulted when the sample was stressed with a faster rising voltage, although the peak voltage (considered here to be the breakdown vol tage) was increased by only a small amount. Similar results were observed with two different ohmic particles having resistivities of 110 ohm mm and 750 ohm mm which were obtained by crushing carbon-composition resistors. It should be noted that breakdown in the case of the zinc oxide sample occurred at a voltage which exceeded the expected varistor turn-on level by a factor of two or three. The important role of a gas discharge in the breakdown mechanism was verified by repeating these measurements with the sample immersed in freon gas, which raised the breakdown voltage significantly.

articleTitle: Comparison of dc and 60 Hz ac positive and negative partial discharge inceptions in SF6
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The problem of defining partial discharge (corona) inception in electronegative gases, such as SF<inf>6</inf> and its mixtures with other gases, has not yet been satisfactorily resolved, partly because of a lack of fundamental information about the nature of corona characteristics under a variety of operating conditions. To arrive at a consistent definition for inception requires an understanding of factors that affect the development of corona near onset, one being the waveform of the applied voltage. We report here comparative measurements of dc and 60-Hz ac corona inceptions in SF<inf>6</inf> in an attempt to determine the extent to which measurements performed under dc conditions are indicative of what might occur under ac conditions.

articleTitle: Inception and suppression of bow-tie treeing caused by metallic contaminants in crosslinked polyethylene
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Some experiments were performed on XLPE sheets containing a definite amount of Cu powder, water-soluble Cu<sup>+</sup> or Cu<sup>++</sup> compounds, or organocopper complexes in order to elucidate the advantageous effect of VS trinity on the suppression of bow-tie trees which had been previously observed in XLPE cable.

articleTitle: The numerical analysis of the thermal pulse experiment
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: 1. The thermal pulse experiment can be put into a quantifiable form. 2. With proper technique, at least ten Fourier coefficients can be obtained for the polarization distribution. This allows changes in polarization that occur within 1/10 of the sample thickness to be seen. 3. For the method used here, all parts of the sample are examined with good resolution. 4. The experiment can reveal meaningful results that can lead to understanding of the poling process in polymers.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated polarization and temperature dependence of equilibrium polarization in polymers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The theoretical formulation of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) of dipolar systems is usually restricted to the case that the equilibrium polarization Pe depends on the temperature according to the Langevin function and that this temperature dependence can be neglected during the nonisothermal step of the poling process (i.e., the frozen-in polarization of the sample before a TSDC experiment is started is considered as equal to the equilibrium polarization obtained at the polarizing temperature T<inf>p</inf>).<sup>1</sup> For a single relaxation time, this leads to the familiar Bucci-Fieschi equation representing an asymmetrical “glow curve,” the area of which can then be directly related to relaxation parameters such as dipole moment and dipole density.<sup>2</sup> With the same basic assumptions, the classical theory of thermally stimulated polarization currents (TSPC) provides for obtaining current peaks characterized by the same position, height, and shape as the corresponding TSDC peaks, the only difference being that the polarization current is of opposite sign.

articleTitle: Dielectric response of doped ICE measured with linear blocking layers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: These experiments support the assumption of linearity and the equivalent circuit of Fig. 1. Further work is needed to ascertain whether a different equivalent circuit might not fit the data even better. The question of frequency-distributed relaxation processes in ice and of the physical nature of different relaxation processes should be investigated by means of equivalent-circuit theory and fitting.

articleTitle: Thermally stimulated conductivity in electron irradiated FEP-Teflon
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: A great deal of experimental work has been done on the electrical properties of the co-polymer FEP-Teflon,<sup>1–4</sup> mainly because of the promise which it shows as a charge storage medium. Yet the correct interpretation of the data, obtained mainly from thermally stimulated conductivity (TSC) and transient radiation-induced conductivity measurements, is far from obvious. Whilst it is generally accepted that holes are much more mobile than electrons in FEP-Teflon, the identity of the traps which control the hole mobility is as yet unknown, and a “direct” measurement of that mobility, using the time-of-flight technique, has been reported only once.

articleTitle: Interfacial phenomena at electrode-nylon 6 at temperatures 80–120 °C
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: A close examination of the step response current i(t) of nylon 6 allows one to identify the absorption and quasi-steady state conduction currents. The total absorption charge tends to saturate with rising temperature or applied field and is almost independent of electrode metals. These results can be interpreated in terms of the immigration of the fixed number of ions existing in polymer toward the counter electrode. It is also suggested from the ohmic nature of the conduction current that the accumulated ions hardly establish the space charge but are likely neutralized at the electrodes. In contrast to no difference in the absorption charge between gold and aluminum electrodes, the discharged charge with gold electrodes is greater than that with aluminum ones. It is also shown that the state of neutralized ions depends on the electric field and the period for which the absorption has been made. It is also clarified that the accumulated neutralized charges scarcely discharge at T<inf>f</inf>, but the ionization rate is promoted at a higher temperature than T<inf>f</inf>.

articleTitle: Nonlinear bipolar conduction with sinusoidal voltage excitations
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: A drift dominated conduction model is often used in the analysis of charge transport through a dielectric where the velocities of charge carriers are proportional to the local electric field through their mobilities. In return the electric field is also related to the carrier charge densities through Gauss's law. Using this conduction model recent work has developed a generalized method which solves for the electric field and space charge distributions and the time dependence of the terminal current for any initial and boundary conditions with any terminal excitation or constraint.<sup>1–5</sup> While this past work has emphasized the transient response to a step voltage, in this study we consider a sinusoidally varying applied voltage for bipolar conduction including Langevin recombination<sup>6</sup> and also consider the effects of a lossy dielectric with ohmic conductivity. Analytical solutions for the terminal current are compared to preliminary experiments.

articleTitle: The surge characteristics of electrical insulation operating at cryogenic temperatures
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The short term and long term impulse breakdown characteristics of Nomex, Tyvek, and PPLP immersed in pressurized LN<inf>2</inf> at 77.3 K have been investigated. The breakdown strength is dependent on the structure of the material and on its resistance to partial discharges. The breakdown strengths of the fibrous materials improves slightly and that of PPLP remains constant with increasing pressure of the LN<inf>2</inf> up to 0.4 MPa. The 250/2500 µs breakdown strengths of the tested insulation systems are up to 15% higher than those for 1.2/50 µs impulses. A similar result is observed for the repeated impulse tests, the difference being about 25% for PPLP.

articleTitle: E. S. R. study of CU2+ in polyethylene containing electrical and water trees introduction
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Treeing phenomena, manifestations of polymer degradation due to electrical stress, are of much concern in cable technology using polymeric insulation. For several years<sup>1–3</sup> we have been using electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy in an attempt to gain better insight into physico-chemical changes taking place in electrical trees (and breakdown channels) in polyethylene (PE).

articleTitle: Test of a model for the humidity dependence of resistance
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: An empirical summation of resistance data has previously been rationalized using an electrostatic model for charge transport in polymers above their glass transition temperature. This rationale depended on estimates of intrinsic material properties to support its credibility. This present work attempts to support the model with directly measured extrinsic properties.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of cable processing
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Electrochemical or water treeing is currently the major long term materials problem associated with the use of crosslinked polyethylene for insulating electrical distribution cables.

articleTitle: Problems in the determination of anisotropic transport properties in very thin polymer fibers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The technological need often arises to know the conductivity of a thin fiber. There are numerous references in the literature to the conductivity of fibers but when one looks in detail at these references it is found that the measurements have been made on woven fabrics or mats of fibers.

articleTitle: The influence of PD-stabilization on space charge and aging effects of polymers
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Therefore, one of the conclusions which can be drawn is that PD-power correlated to the stressed area describes deterioration mechanisms much better than PD-energy, because of the random geometric scatter of the discharges (Figure 3).

articleTitle: The effect of field dependent mobility on instabilities associated with space charge enhanced conduction
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Previous calculations<sup>1, 2</sup> investigated the instability associated with space charge enhanced emission from the cathode into a dielectric solid, the space charge in the solid arising primarily from collision ionization. Both plane and spherical geometry were considered, with spherical geometry probably giving a better representation of avalanche buildup. Current work extends the calculations by investigating the effects of variations in hole mobility, geometric field enhancement, and layered structure between anode and cathode. The model is not an avalanche model, but a steady state collision ionization model that results in a current controlled instability.

articleTitle: Elastomer dielectric for pulse power
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: In practice, the use of an elastomer dielectric has allowed us to construct a pulser one order of magnitude smaller than predecessors having the same output characteristics. Additionally, the elastomer dielectric used in pulse power systems leads to improved production techniques and improved system reliability.

articleTitle: Examination of field-aged insulation for changes in molecular structure
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The GPC results for samples taken from along the cable and with radius suggest that some very minor changes in the molecular weight distribution have taken place with aging. The changes are too small to affect the physical properties of the insulation and would not be normally connected either with large chemical or bulk electrical changes. This then appears to exclude the possibility of uniform molecular degradation as a necessary preliminary to the very local changes associated with dielectric breakdown, unless the aging process can vary significantly over distances of a meter or less. Further efforts will be directed at finding such “hotspots”, if they indeed exist, and at improving the precision of the techniques for detecting molecular weight changes.

articleTitle: Effect of morphology on some electrical properties of PE film
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Experiment has not revealed a systematic variation of either E<inf>I</inf> or J<inf>S</inf> with ρ, although the prestress effect, [(E<inf>I</inf>−E<inf>p−</inf>)/E<inf>p−</inf>] %, seems to vary linearly. This is thought to be fortu1touS. Bradwell et al.<sup>5</sup> attributed breakdown to the establishment of a critical field at the cathode and conditioning to the modification of the cathode field by space charge, dependent on the conductivity. The present result is consistent with this. The negative effect exhibited by Rigidex 3 and Rigidex 9 implies formation of negative rather than positive space charge in front of that electrode which changes from anode to cathode with application of the impulse, and hence a different mechanism of conduction from other grades of PE.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of substituted carboxylic acids
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The series of chloromethylacetic acids was studied because trimethylacetic acid, also called pivalic acid, had an interesting dielectric behaviour. Since the substitution of chloro- for methyl- groups had been interesting for other compounds, it was expected to show a trend of properties for this series due to the effect of the chloro groups on the carboxyl part of the molecules. Unexpectedly, the feature expected to show the most effect of the substitution, the phase II-phase I transition in pivalic acid, ceased to exist in the chloro compounds.

articleTitle: Theory of dielectric relaxation in blocking contact MIM structures
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Metal-insulator or metal-amorphous semiconductor blocking contacts are important because of their potential solar cell applications.<sup>1, 2</sup> However, these structures are still not well understood even for crystalline materials,<sup>3</sup> while the case of amorphous material is even more uncertain and poorly understood. In most cases, only steady state characteristics of these structures are studied. This can provide limited information. Characteristics before the current becomes constant can provide information on a wider scale, and thus assumptions on metal-insulator structure can be judged more critically. The theory of dielectric relaxation for MIM structures was first formulated by Simmons and Taylor.<sup>4</sup> As recently pointed out by us,<sup>5</sup> this theory can explain the experimental results only qualitatively. Thus the correctness of the assumptions of the theory and the conclusions drawn from it are doubtful. We feel that it is still necessary to know the charge conduction mechanism in such structures. The object of the present paper is to discuss the theory of isothermal dielectric relaxation in blocking contact metal-insula tor-metal structures considering various possible assumptions.

articleTitle: Charge storage in polyvinyledene fluoride electret
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: It is well established that pyroelectricity in polyvinylidene fluoride (PVF<inf>2</inf>) is significiantly enhanced on the application of a suitably high electric field at an elevated temperature for an extended period of time (i.e. poling). This induced effect, which may be quite stable at ordinary temperatures, will be superimposed on any inherent pyroelectricity of the materia11 A pyroelectric coefficient, as high as 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup> Cm<sup>−2</sup>K<sup>−1</sup> may be obtained with prestretched and poled PVF<inf>2</inf>. The possible origins of pyroelectricity in PVF<inf>2</inf> are<sup>1</sup>: (i) the temperature dependence of spontaneous polarization, (ii) a coupling of non-uniform temperature dependence of permittivity with the trapped charges and (iii) a combination of (i) and (ii). The time dependent charge transport properties of insulating polymers may be studied by the transient charging and discharging currents at different temperatures and fields. On the application of a high dc step field, the charging (polarizing)current decay as a function of t<sup>−n</sup> where t is time and n is a number, until a quasi-steady state conduction current is reached. If the sample is then short circuited, then the discharge (depolarizing) current tends to be a mirror image of the charging current for low temperatures and fields. .For high temperatures and fields this mirror image nature of the charging and discharging currents is no longer maintained. The charge transport and the polarising mechanisms in the low temperature range, including the glass transition temperature are of considerable interest in semi-crystalline polymers. The present work reports results of a study of slow pyroelectric responses during the depolarization (short circuited condition) of a previously charged PVF<inf>2</inf> electret in the temperature range of −60°c to +20°c.

articleTitle: Dielectric measurements on particles using dielectrophoretic levitation
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Both analytical and experimental results indicate the sensitivity of dielectrophoretic levitation to the shape and spacing of electrodes. In selection of an electrode configuration, several factors are important. First, the range of realizable static levitation positions between the release point and the field null must be maximized. The result is increased sensitivity of the measurement and improved visibility of levitated particles or bubbles. Second, the “voltage efficiency” must be good. Good voltage efficiency means that particles can be levitated without recourse to excessively high voltages. For an electrode configuration such as the ring/plane system of Figure 2, where an approximate analytical solution is possible, the various tradeoffs can be examined employing a desk-top calculator with an x−y plotter. Despite some deficiencies in the analytical expression, i.e., Equation (5), the trends and tradeoffs identified by the analysis are verified by experimental measurement. For more practical electrode configurations such as those depicted in Figure 5, an experimental approach is the only convenient way to determine performance. Of the configurations tested so far, that shown in Figure 5b seems to be best. While its voltage efficiency is only 94%,compared to an equivalent ring/plane system, it does offer much better sensitivity and more convenient particle visibility (unobscured by any electrode structure). Other interesting electrode structures come to mind, and these all require the same experimental approach of mapping out the electric field gradient (∂E<inf>Z</inf><sup>1</sup>/∂z) before their merits can be assessed.

articleTitle: Optical measurements of electrical conduction in liquefied nitrogen
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The prebreakdown phonomena in liquefied nitrogen have been studied by using the modified optical Schlieren technique with an image-converter camera to examine optically the drift velocities of the disturbance due to the movement of the charged carriers. Consequently, the drift velocity of the charged carrier in liquefied nitrogen was observed as the Schlieren image. At the same time, the prebreakdown current corresponding to the movement of the disturbance was measured using optoelectronic techniques. The mobility of the disturbance obtained in our experiment was 1 ∼ 4 × 10<sup>−1</sup> cm<sup>2</sup>/V•s.

articleTitle: Electron transport in cryogenic liquids: Nitrogen
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The continuing study of electron transport in insulating liquids has been extended to nitrogen. Although attempts to measure the mobility of electrons in liquid nitrogen have been made previously,<sup>1</sup> it was suggested that the species measured were anions.<sup>1, 2</sup> If such is the case, it is important to determine whether the electrons were captured by impurities or by the nitrogen itself.

articleTitle: Electrical breakdown strength and morphology of amorphous part in elongated polyethylene
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The electronic thermal breakdown may occur in the amorphous phase of low-density polyethylene which consists of half amorphous and half crystalline regions. The breakdown strength is affected by a change in the morphology of the amorphous parts by the elongation of samples having different M.I.

articleTitle: The effect of water on the physical aging of poly (vinyl acetate)
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Only water in a bound state affects the glass transition behavior in PVAc. The water plasticizes the transition lowering T<inf>g</inf> but does not affect the distribution of relaxation times. In addition, PVAc's physical aging at a constant temperature increment, ΔT, below its T<inf>g</inf> is found to be independent of water content.

articleTitle: A thermal model and its application to semiconductively glazed insulators
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: If the thermal effect of semiconductive1y glazed insulator is to keep the whole insulator dry in a moist environment, the thermal model can be used to design an insulator glaze which minimizes total power loss without any unacceptable compromise in reliability.

articleTitle: High temperature electrical insulation properties of polypyromellitimide and aromatic polyamide fibres/epoxy resin composites
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Polypyromellitimide, aromatic polyamide, and epoxy resin have been used as high temperature electrical insulating materials.

articleTitle: Insulating coatings on electrodes in transformer oil
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: The work has demonstrated that oil purity is undoubtedly the most important single variable in determining the insulation strength with both coated and uncoated electrodes. The rapid deterioration in strength observed in newly purified oil is believed to be due to contamination by atmospheric moisture and is therefore unlikely to be experienced to the same degree in closed systems.

articleTitle: Distribution of electron avalanches in SF6
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Electrical discharges in gases originate when conditions permit the development of ionization. Such ionization can occur in pressurized gases when electric fields cause free electrons to gain sufficient energy between impacts with gas molecules. The progressive development of field-driven ionization, the electron avalanche, increases or decreases along the path to the anode according to the field intensity.

articleTitle: Deterioration of polyethylene due to gaseous discharge products
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: NO<inf>2</inf>, N<inf>2</inf>O, and RNO<inf>3</inf> are generated mainly by the corona discharge in air. The production of RNO<inf>3</inf> and NO<inf>2</inf> was periodic with time. The periodic characteristics were found to be a function of humidity and temperature of the air. The RNO<inf>3</inf> is found to affect the deterioration of polyethylene.

articleTitle: Carrier traps in vapor-deposited poly-p-xylylene films
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Carrier traps in vapor-deposited PPX were discussed from the analyses of X-ray induced TSC and TL. There were five TSC peaks and two TL peaks in the temperature range of −180°C to 150°C. The lower two TSC and two TL peaks were related to the local mode relaxations of CH2 and phenylene units. One of the remaining TSC peaks was considered to be associated with the glass transition and the others had nothing to do with the molecular motions. These two peaks were significantly affected by the crystallographic transformation which could be initiated by thermal annealing at 230°C.

articleTitle: On the unifying admittance calculation simultaneously commenting on H. Schering's conceptyon δ = 90 - |φ|
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: • If problems of insulation in electrical engineering are treated strictly by unifying impedance calculations, dissipation factors must be negative values. This can be proven by the results obtained by H. Schering.<sup>1, 2</sup> The fact that for half a century no negative dissipation factors have ever been seen shows that in the field of insulation in electrical engineering this kind of calculation has in reality been foregone.

articleTitle: Generalized box model for electron irradia ted teflon foils
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Radiation-induced charge storage and conduction processes in solid dielectrics [I], such as Teflon, have both theoretical and practical significance. Generalized models have been developed to describe the externally measured currents or voltages under different modes of poling. They take into account range straggling [2] and use realistic expressions for electron absorption, charge deposition, energy deposition, and dose rate as functions of space [3].

articleTitle: Dependence of surface electron dynamics on beam current density and energy in electron-beam experiments
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: In this paper, we examine some effects of electron transport and dynamics in Kapton and Teflon thin films irradiated with an electron beam. In these experiments, a thin, metal-backed dielectric film such as those used for thermal control on spacecraft is exposed to a mono-energetic electron beam.<sup>1, 2</sup> Currents to the chamber walls and through the sample are measured. The current measured to the metalized back of the sample is made up of the displacement current as charge builds up in the sample and of the leakage current through the sample. When equilibrium is established, the current to the metalized back of the sample is just the leakage through the sample. (The leakage current in a material that obeys Ohm's law will depend linearly on the electric field in the dielectric.) Electrons trapped on or near the surface of the sample and the charges they induce on the metalized back of the sample produce an electric field through the sample. The potential on the surface of the sample is measured with a noncontacting voltage probe.

articleTitle: Measurement of voltage-induced charge distributions in pet filbs
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Significant negative ionic space charge occur in PET films poled by fields as low as 0.14 MV/em at 420°K. The negative charge lies adjacent to the anode and results in a highly distorted electric field distribution which, at the anode, can be several times greater than the applied field strength. The anode is blocking to this negative ionic charge which can be discharged primarily by carrier movement through the cathode.

articleTitle: Transport processes in polymeric solids - the role of the surface and the electrodes
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: A non-contacting high definition induction probe surface-potential monitor, together with pulsed corona charging, produces a versatile tool for the study of both dielectric and conduction processes in highly insulating solids and is capable of yielding data of good accuracy under conditions not easily attainable, if at all, by conventional techniques. Moreover, the influence of metal electrodes can be determined with great clarity. Theoretical treatment of the results permits a new insight into the detailed mechanisms of both polarization and conduction processes.

articleTitle: Whitehead Memorial Lecture: Interface effects in the electrical response of non-metallic conducting solids and liquids
publicationTitle: Conference on Electrical Insulation & Dielectric Phenomena - Annual Report 1980
abstract: Two of the recent J. B. Whitehead Memorial Lecturers, J. G. Trump and Bernhard Gross, have discussed Whitehead the man, and Gross has touched on Whitehead's work on the anomalous properties of dielectrics, emphasizing and reiterating Whitehead's feeling about the great divergence between the points of view of experimentalists and theorists in the field.
